programmes.amount_note: Accelerator funding for deep tech companies; amount set per call.
programmes.reopen_note: Business Finland's 2026 funding overview describes the Deep Tech Accelerator as temporarily closed, with an announcement of possible new calls pending.
programmes.source_snippet: Deep Tech Accelerator - Temporarily closed; announcement of possible new calls pending.

programmes.amount_note: Staged funding for young innovative companies; historically up to around EUR 1.25 million across phases as a mix of grant and loan.
programmes.deadline_note: NIY remains closed to new applications.
programmes.reopen_note: Business Finland's 2026 funding overview states NIY remains closed due to state budget cuts, affecting new applications only; existing projects continue. No reopening date published.
programmes.source_snippet: NIY Funding - Remains closed due to state budget cuts (affecting new applications only).

programmes.amount_note: Grant or loan for company R&D projects; grant share typically 40-50% of project costs for SMEs, loans up to 70%.
Funding for research teams to commercialise research results and prepare a spinout; grant covers a high share of project costs for research organisations.

eligibility.other_note: Business Finland's 2026 overview states Research to Business continues with an increased funding allocation.

programmes.amount_note: Maximum EUR 100,000; funding covers 75% of the project's approved total costs.
programmes.deadline_note: The single-round Sprint Grant call closed 31 August 2026. Business Finland's own call page states a continuous call begins 1 September 2026 with no fixed closing date.

procedure_steps.detail: Register in the My Business Finland service
Book an appointment with a Business Finland advisor before applying
Submit the application in the funding e-service with project plan, financial statements and business plan

eligibility.other_note: Minimum equity investment of at least EUR 50,000 in the balance sheet, paid to the company in cash. No prior Business Finland funding (or a significant change of business based on a new innovation). Replaces Tempo funding.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum amount of funding is EUR 100,000. The funding covers 75% of the project's approved total costs.

programmes.amount_note: Maximum grant EUR 60,000 covering 75% of project costs (max EUR 80,000 total project). Paid 70% in advance.
programmes.deadline_note: The Tempo application period closed in October 2025. Final deadline was 3 October 2025.
programmes.reopen_note: Business Finland states Tempo is permanently closed and will not reopen. Its successor is the Sprint Grant (max EUR 100,000, 75% coverage), piloted from early 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Required a committed team of at least 2 people working in Finland, EUR 38,000 total funding of which at least EUR 30,000 equity.

programmes.source_snippet: The Tempo funding application period has closed in October 2025 for the time being.

programmes.amount_note: Energy aid for investment and audit projects in Finland that improve energy efficiency and savings or promote new energy technology; available to companies and organisations of all sizes. Minimum investment costs EUR 10,000 (energy efficiency) or EUR 30,000 (other).
programmes.deadline_note: Most Business Finland instruments accept applications continuously; some thematic calls have fixed deadlines.
programmes.source_snippet: Energy aid is available for companies and organizations of all sizes to support investments and audit projects that improve energy efficiency and savings.

programmes.funder: ELY-keskus (Centre for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment)
programmes.amount_note: Development grant for SME growth and internationalisation projects; grant share depends on region, company size and project type.

programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with the national space agency or regional co-funder
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation with technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support. Some national BICs add local top-up funding.
programmes.deadline_note: This ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. Contact the local centre for the next deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss suitability
Submit application documents before the local deadline
Tender Opening Board review, then presentation to the Tender Evaluation Board
Register a company in Finland before signing the incubation contract

eligibility.other_note: Business must use space-based systems, apply space technology in a non-space domain, or develop products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in Finland.

programmes.source_snippet: Up to two years of business incubation at an ESA BIC of your choice. Technical support from leading experts in the region and from ESA. Business coaching.

programmes.amount_note: Investment prize funded by a syndicate of investors, historically around EUR 1m as a convertible note or equity round
programmes.deadline_note: Applications typically open in the summer and close in the early autumn, ahead of the November Slush conference in Helsinki
programmes.reopen_note: Runs each year alongside Slush in Helsinki in November. Applications usually open around June or July.

eligibility.other_note: Early-stage startups worldwide, typically pre-Series A. Founders must attend Slush in Helsinki.

programmes.amount_note: Guarantee covering at most 80% of a bank loan; minimum guarantee EUR 10,000 and up to EUR 160,000 in total per enterprise; no self-financing contribution required; guarantors cover 25% of the guarantee amount (min EUR 3,000).
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; applied for through the bank. Applications processed within three banking days.

eligibility.other_note: Finnish companies or registered private entrepreneurs (not cooperatives or registered associations); new SMEs. Contains de minimis aid.

programmes.source_snippet: Finnvera’s Start Guarantee helps new SMEs to obtain bank financing for various investment and working capital needs.

programmes.amount_note: Guarantee covering usually 50-80% of a loan or other financing commitment, determined case by case; minimum guarantee EUR 10,000; secures domestic bank financing for investments, working capital and business acquisitions.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; applied for via Finnvera's online service after discussion with the bank.

eligibility.other_note: Intended especially for SMEs with fewer than 250 employees and turnover up to EUR 50 million or balance sheet up to EUR 43 million; larger companies only on special grounds.

programmes.source_snippet: Finnvera Guarantee is intended for SMEs as security for domestic financing in such areas as investments, working capital and business and company acquisitions.

programmes.amount_note: Personal loan to an entrepreneur, minimum EUR 20,000; loan period typically 5-6 years (maximum 12 years); interest is six-month Euribor plus fixed margin of 3.75% p.a. plus a management fee.

eligibility.other_note: Borrower must hold at least 5% of share capital and votes after the investment, work in the company or serve on its board, and have personal finances in good order. Lent to the founder personally to invest equity in the company.

programmes.source_snippet: An Entrepreneur Loan is a personal loan granted to an entrepreneur. It may be used, for example, for acquiring shares in a public limited company or making an investment in the share capital.

programmes.amount_note: Loan of EUR 20,000-50,000; maximum loan period 5 years with up to one year instalment-free; interest six-month Euribor plus 4.5% p.a.; 1.5% service fee on withdrawal.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted from 1 February 2026 in the Finnvera online service; no closing date published.

eligibility.other_note: Enterprises with fewer than ten employees and annual turnover or balance sheet up to EUR 2 million; each enterprise may receive the loan only once; start-ups also eligible from February 2026.

programmes.source_snippet: Enterprises with 1–9 employees may apply for a loan for growth and enhanced productivity from 1 February 2026.

programmes.name_local: Partnership model funding: Co-Innovation and Research, development and piloting
programmes.amount_note: Continuous partnership-model funding for joint company projects and company-research organisation projects in leading companies' ecosystem themes; funding can also be granted to individual companies' own R&D projects.
programmes.deadline_note: Call open with application deadline 31.12.2030; apply continuously.

eligibility.other_note: Companies (including SMEs joining ecosystem partnerships) and research organisations; Co-Innovation joint project between companies or between companies and research organisations, or a company's own R&D project.

programmes.source_snippet: Continuous call from 31.1.2024 for companies and research organizations.
